# Kubelet Drop-in Configuration

KubeSolo generates the kubelet configuration on every start. To change kubelet settings that the KubeSolo config file doesn't cover, such as eviction thresholds or image garbage collection, write a drop-in file. The kubelet loads drop-ins on top of KubeSolo's generated configuration.

---

## How It Works

On every start, KubeSolo writes the kubelet configuration to:

```
/var/lib/kubesolo/kubelet/config/config.yaml
```

**Do not edit this file.** KubeSolo overwrites it on every start, so any changes you make there are lost on the next restart.

Instead, put drop-in files in:

```
/var/lib/kubesolo/kubelet/config.d/
```

If you run KubeSolo with `--path`, the directory is `<path>/kubelet/config.d/`. KubeSolo creates it on every start.

The kubelet merges every `*.conf` file in the directory, including subdirectories, on top of the generated configuration in file-name order. A file loaded later overrides one loaded earlier, so a numeric prefix such as `10-` or `99-` controls which file wins.

Settings are merged key by key. For example, a drop-in that sets one `evictionHard` threshold changes that threshold only, and the others keep their defaults. Lists are the exception: a list in a drop-in replaces the whole list.

The kubelet reads drop-ins only at startup. After you add or change one, restart KubeSolo:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart kubesolo
```

### Drop-in format

Each drop-in is a `KubeletConfiguration` that sets only the fields you want to change:

```yaml
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: KubeletConfiguration
# settings to change
```

- The file name must end in `.conf`. The kubelet ignores any other file, and KubeSolo logs a warning when it finds one.
- `apiVersion` and `kind` are required. KubeSolo refuses to start when a drop-in doesn't set them, or isn't valid YAML, and names the file in its log.
- The kubelet ignores fields it doesn't recognise without reporting an error, so check field names carefully. [Checking the Result](#checking-the-result) shows how to confirm a setting took effect.

See the [KubeletConfiguration reference](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/config-api/kubelet-config.v1beta1/) for every available field.

---

## Examples

### Eviction thresholds and image garbage collection

By default the kubelet reports DiskPressure when less than 15% of the image filesystem is free. On a single node that is usually the root filesystem, so on a large disk the default reserves a lot of space. Once DiskPressure is reported, the kubelet evicts pods and rejects new ones until the disk is freed, and a single node has nowhere else to run them.

Create `/var/lib/kubesolo/kubelet/config.d/10-eviction.conf`:

```yaml
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: KubeletConfiguration
evictionHard:
  imagefs.available: "10%"
  nodefs.available: "5%"
evictionPressureTransitionPeriod: 1m
imageGCHighThresholdPercent: 80
imageGCLowThresholdPercent: 70
```

Keep `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` below the disk usage that triggers `imagefs.available`, so the kubelet removes unused images before it starts evicting pods.

### Memory on small devices

The default `memory.available` threshold is `100Mi`. On a device with 512 MB of RAM that is about 20% of memory. To lower it, create `/var/lib/kubesolo/kubelet/config.d/10-memory.conf`:

```yaml
apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: KubeletConfiguration
evictionHard:
  memory.available: "50Mi"
```

---

## Checking the Result

After restarting KubeSolo, check that it loaded each drop-in:

```bash
sudo journalctl -u kubesolo | grep "kubelet drop-in"
```

Then ask the kubelet for the configuration it is running with:

```bash
PKI=/var/lib/kubesolo/pki
sudo curl -s --cacert $PKI/ca/ca.crt --cert $PKI/admin/admin.crt --key $PKI/admin/admin.key \
  https://127.0.0.1:10250/configz \
  | jq '.kubeletconfig | {evictionHard, imageGCHighThresholdPercent, imageGCLowThresholdPercent}'
```

---

## Settings KubeSolo Manages

Some settings can't be changed with a drop-in, or shouldn't be.

**Refused.** KubeSolo refuses to start when a drop-in sets any of these. It logs the file and setting, then stops; under systemd it is restarted and stops again until you fix or remove the file. Use the [configuration file](config-file.md) instead:

| Setting | Use instead |
|---|---|
| `cpuManagerPolicy` | `kubernetes.kubelet.cpuManager.policy` |
| `cpuManagerPolicyOptions` | `kubernetes.kubelet.cpuManager.policyOptions` |
| `reservedSystemCPUs` | `kubernetes.kubelet.cpuManager.reservedCPUs` |

When the CPU manager settings change, KubeSolo removes the kubelet's CPU manager state so the kubelet can start with the new settings. It can't detect a change made in a drop-in. See [CPU pinning](cpu-pinning.md).

**Warned.** KubeSolo sets these itself and logs a warning when a drop-in overrides them, because the node may stop working:

- `containerRuntimeEndpoint`
- `authentication` and `authorization`
- `tlsCertFile` and `tlsPrivateKeyFile`
- `cgroupDriver`
- `clusterDNS` and `clusterDomain`
- `resolvConf`
- In [container mode](container-mode.md): `cgroupsPerQOS` and `enforceNodeAllocatable`

---

## Container Mode

In container mode, the drop-in directory is inside the KubeSolo data volume. Write the drop-in into the container, then restart it:

```bash
docker exec -i kubesolo sh -c 'cat > /var/lib/kubesolo/kubelet/config.d/10-eviction.conf' < 10-eviction.conf
docker restart kubesolo
```

In container mode KubeSolo sets its own `evictionHard` thresholds, with the disk thresholds at `0%`, and sets `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` to `100`. A drop-in that sets these fields overrides KubeSolo's values, key by key.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| A setting has no effect | The file doesn't end in `.conf`, KubeSolo wasn't restarted after the change, or the field name is misspelled. The kubelet ignores fields it doesn't recognise. Check the log for `applying kubelet drop-in`, then check the field name against the KubeletConfiguration reference. |
| KubeSolo stops at startup with `must set apiVersion: kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 and kind: KubeletConfiguration` | The named drop-in is missing those fields, or sets a different `kind`. |
| KubeSolo stops at startup with `sets cpuManagerPolicy` | Move the CPU manager settings to the KubeSolo configuration file. See [Settings KubeSolo Manages](#settings-kubesolo-manages). |
| The node is `NotReady` and the log shows `kubelet exited with error: failed to merge kubelet configs` | A drop-in sets a value of the wrong type, for example a string where the kubelet expects a number. The error names the field. Fix the drop-in and restart KubeSolo. |
| Edits to `/var/lib/kubesolo/kubelet/config/config.yaml` disappear | KubeSolo regenerates that file on every start. Use a drop-in instead. |
